title: Carry scan output
statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a set, let $\operatorname{top}:\Gamma\to\{\mathrm{true},\mathrm{false}\}$ and $\operatorname{next}:\Gamma\to\Gamma$, and let $w$ be a finite word over $\Gamma$. Consider a two-pass scan that starts with a true carry, scans left to right changing a symbol to $\operatorname{next}(\gamma)$ while the carry is true and setting the carry to $\operatorname{top}(\gamma)$, then scans the resulting word right to left without changing its symbols. Its final state is the conjunction of $\operatorname{top}$ over $w$, and its output word consists of the symbols in the initial consecutive $\operatorname{top}$-true prefix changed by $\operatorname{next}$, followed by the first symbol after that prefix changed by $\operatorname{next}$ if one exists, followed by the remaining symbols unchanged.
